blocks.text: The **Western Chalukyas of Kalyani (973–1189 CE)**, who revived Chalukya power after overthrowing the Rashtrakutas, waged a long rivalry with the **Cholas** and fostered a **Kannada-Sanskrit cultural flowering** — including **Vijnaneshwara's Mitakshara**, the classic law digest.

rows: **Vikramaditya VI** — started the **Chalukya-Vikrama era**; patron of **Bilhana (Vikramankadevacharita)** & **Vijnaneshwara**.
Continuous wars with the **Cholas** over Vengi & the Tungabhadra doab.
**Vijnaneshwara's Mitakshara** — a commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti; foundational Hindu law.

items: **Western/Kalyani Chalukyas (973–1189 CE)**, capital **Kalyani (Basavakalyan)**; founder **Tailapa II** (overthrew the Rashtrakutas); long rivalry with the **Cholas** over Vengi & the Tungabhadra doab.

**Vikramaditya VI** — greatest; started the **Chalukya-Vikrama era**; his court poet **Bilhana** wrote **Vikramankadevacharita**; jurist **Vijnaneshwara** wrote the **Mitakshara** (a commentary on Yajnavalkya — the leading Hindu law text on inheritance).
**Art**: mature **Vesara** temples — **Mahadeva temple, Itagi** ('Emperor among temples'), Kasivishveshwara (Lakkundi), Dodda Basappa (Dambal); Kannada & Sanskrit literature flourished.
The **Basava/Lingayat (Veerashaiva)** movement arose in this milieu (12th c) — Basavanna's social-reform Bhakti.
Tailapa II founder; Vikramaditya VI greatest (Chalukya-Vikrama era, Bilhana, Vijnaneshwara).
Mitakshara (Vijnaneshwara) is the must-know legal contribution.

**Vikramaditya VI** — greatest; started the **Chalukya-Vikrama era**.

glossary.definition: Vijnaneshwara's authoritative commentary on the Yajnavalkya Smriti, a foundation of Hindu inheritance law.
A calendar era instituted by Vikramaditya VI of Kalyani.

blocks.text: The **Imperial Cholas (850–1279 CE)** built south India's greatest empire, famed for a **remarkable system of village self-government, a powerful navy, Dravidian temple architecture (Brihadeshwara) and Chola bronzes (Nataraja)**. **Rajaraja I** and **Rajendra I** carried Chola power overseas to **Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia**.

rows: **Rajaraja I** (Brihadeshwara temple, Tanjore; conquered Sri Lanka), **Rajendra I** ('Gangaikonda Chola'; naval raid on **Srivijaya/Southeast Asia**; Ganga expedition).
**Uttaramerur inscriptions** detail the **village assembly (Sabha/Ur) & committees (variyams)** — the celebrated Chola local democracy.
Empire → **mandalam → valanadu → nadu → ur**; land survey & revenue.
Strongest Indian navy; overseas conquests (Sri Lanka, Maldives, Srivijaya).

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: the Imperial Cholas

items: **Cholas (850–1279 CE)** revived by **Vijayalaya** (Tanjore); greatest — **Rajaraja I** (built the **Brihadeeswara/Rajarajeswara temple, Thanjavur** — UNESCO; conquered Sri Lanka, Maldives) & **Rajendra I** (title **Gangaikonda Chola**; naval expedition to **Srivijaya (SE Asia)**; new capital **Gangaikonda Cholapuram**).

**Local self-government** — the exam jewel: the **Uttaramerur inscriptions (Parantaka I)** detail the **Kudavolai** (pot-ticket lottery) election of village assemblies — **Ur** (general), **Sabha/Mahasabha** (brahmadeya villages) & **Nagaram** (merchants); committees (**variyams**) for tanks, gardens, justice.

**Administration**: provinces = **Mandalam → Valanadu → Nadu → village**; land survey & revenue; strong **navy**; **Kaikkola** & **Valangai/Idangai** (right/left-hand) caste guilds; merchant guilds (**Ayyavole/Manigramam**).

**Art**: **Dravidian temple** apex — soaring **vimanas** (Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Airavatesvara-Darasuram = the 'Great Living Chola Temples', UNESCO); superb **Chola bronzes** (**Nataraja** — lost-wax); Tamil Shaiva **Nayanars** & Vaishnava **Alvars** canonised (Nalayira Divya Prabandham).
Uttaramerur inscription = Chola village self-government (Sabha, variyams) — highest-frequency MCQ.
Rajaraja I → Brihadeshwara temple; Rajendra I → Gangaikonda + Srivijaya naval raid.

prelimsPointers: **Rajaraja I** built the **Brihadeshwara (Rajarajeshwara) temple, Tanjore** (UNESCO); conquered Sri Lanka.
**Rajendra I** — title **'Gangaikonda Chola'**; naval expedition against **Srivijaya (SE Asia)**; new capital **Gangaikonda Cholapuram**.

Administrative units — **mandalam → valanadu → nadu → ur**.

The Cholas maintained the **strongest navy** in Indian history.
**Kulottunga I** united the Chola & Eastern Chalukya lines.
**Rajaraja I** built **Brihadeeswara temple, Thanjavur**; **Rajendra I** = **Gangaikonda Chola** (Srivijaya raid).

Assemblies: **Ur, Sabha (brahmadeya), Nagaram (merchants)**; committees = **variyams**.
**Chola bronzes** (Nataraja, lost-wax); Great Living Chola Temples = **UNESCO** (Thanjavur, Gangaikonda Cholapuram, Darasuram).

blocks.text: The **Hoysalas (of Dwarasamudra)** and the **Yadavas (Seunas of Devagiri)** were the two great **12th–14th-century Deccan powers** that succeeded the Chalukyas — the Hoysalas famed for **star-shaped, intricately carved temples**, the Yadavas for **Marathi culture** — both extinguished by the **Delhi Sultanate's Deccan raids (Malik Kafur)**.

rows: Capital **Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)**; greatest **Vishnuvardhana** (converted by Ramanuja); temples at **Belur, Halebidu, Somnathpur** (soapstone, star-shaped).
Capital **Devagiri (Daulatabad)**; greatest **Singhana II**; patrons of **Marathi**; Sangita Ratnakara (Sarngadeva).
Both fell to the **Delhi Sultanate** — **Malik Kafur's raids (1307-11)** under Alauddin Khilji.

sections.heading: 🔎 Exam-ready deep coverage: Hoysalas & Seuna Yadavas

items: **Hoysalas (10th–14th c CE)**, capital **Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)**; rulers Vishnuvardhana, Ballala II; famous for the **star-shaped (stellate) soapstone temples** in the ornate **Hoysala/Vesara** style — **Chennakeshava (Belur), Hoysaleswara (Halebidu), Kesava (Somnathpur)** (recently UNESCO-listed 'Sacred Ensembles of the Hoysalas').
**Ramanuja** (Vishishtadvaita philosopher) influenced Vishnuvardhana (Jain → Vaishnava conversion).

**Seuna Yadavas of Devagiri (12th–14th c)**, capital **Devagiri (Daulatabad)**; scholar **Hemadri** (Chaturvarga Chintamani; the **'Hemadpanthi'** temple style); mathematician **Bhaskaracharya II** (Lilavati) linked to this era.
Both fell to the **Delhi Sultanate** (Alauddin Khilji/Malik Kafur's Deccan raids, early 14th c) — ending the classical South-Indian dynastic order before Vijayanagara.
Hoysalas = Belur/Halebidu/Somnathpur (star-shaped soapstone temples); Vishnuvardhana + Ramanuja.
Yadavas = Devagiri + Marathi; both ended by Malik Kafur's raids.

prelimsPointers: **Hoysala** capital **Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)**; temples at **Belur (Chennakeshava), Halebidu (Hoysaleshwara), Somnathpur**.
**Vishnuvardhana** — greatest Hoysala; influenced by **Ramanuja** (Sri Vaishnavism).
Hoysala temples — **star-shaped (stellate) plan, soapstone, intricate carving**.

Both dynasties were destroyed by **Malik Kafur's Deccan raids (1307-11)** under Alauddin Khilji.
The Hoysala temple ensembles are a **UNESCO World Heritage** listing (2023).

**Ramanuja (Vishishtadvaita)** influenced Hoysala **Vishnuvardhana**.

Both conquered by **Alauddin Khilji / Malik Kafur** (early 14th c).

blocks.text: The **Kakatiyas of Warangal (1163–1323)** and the **Reddi kingdoms (14th–15th c.)** were the great **medieval Telugu (Andhra) powers**. The Kakatiyas built a relatively **open, participatory polity** (including **Rudrama Devi**, a reigning queen) and the **Ramappa/Warangal masterpieces**; the Reddis were noted patrons of **Telugu literature (Srinatha)**.

rows: Capital **Warangal (Orugallu)**; **Ganapatideva** (greatest expansion), **Rudrama Devi** (queen; noted by **Marco Polo**), **Prataparudra** (fell to Delhi 1323).
**Ramappa (Rudreswara) temple — UNESCO**, **Thousand-Pillar temple**, **Warangal kirti-toranas**; nayankara land-service.
**Prolaya Vema Reddy** founded; capitals **Addanki, Kondavidu, Rajahmundry**; patrons of **Srinatha**; forts & temples.
After Kakatiya fall (1323), **Prolaya & Kapaya Nayaka** rallied resistance and briefly freed Warangal.

items: **Kakatiyas of Warangal (Orugallu) (1083–1323 CE)** — unified the Telugu country; rulers **Ganapatideva**, the queen **Rudrama Devi** (one of India's few reigning queens; visited by **Marco Polo**), **Prataparudra II** (fell to the Delhi Sultanate/Ulugh Khan, 1323).

**Legacy**: the **tank-based irrigation** cascade system (Pakhal, Ramappa, Ghanpur lakes → modern **'Mission Kakatiya'**); the **Ramappa (Rudreshwara) temple, Palampet** (**UNESCO 2021** — 'floating' lightweight bricks, dolerite sculptures) & the **Thousand-Pillar Temple** & **Warangal Fort (Kirti Toranas** — Telangana state emblem).

**Reddi kingdoms (1325–1448)** rose after the Kakatiyas (Prolaya Vema Reddi, capital Addanki→Kondaveedu) — revived Telugu culture: **Errana** (completed the Telugu Mahabharatam), **Srinatha** (court poet); rebuilt temples & agraharas.
**Musunuri Nayakas** (Prolaya & Kapaya) briefly recovered Warangal from the Sultanate — early assertion of Telugu political resistance.
Kakatiyas = Warangal, Rudrama Devi (Marco Polo), Ramappa (UNESCO), nayankara.
Reddis = Kondavidu/Rajahmundry, Srinatha; Musunuri Nayakas resisted the Sultanate.
